title: Terraform stability guardrails and version grid for modules/providers
creator: Asha K. Patel
description: Problem: We have seen multiple customer upgrades and on-prem runway incidents caused by unpinned provider changes (aws, azurerm, google) and module inputs that introduce breaking changes when Terraform core versions drift. Goal: Create a single-source-of-truth compatibility grid for Terraform core, major providers, and our private-vpc modules, plus implement enforceable guardrails: provider lockfile strategy, module semver policy, CI health checks and automated canary upgrades. This ticket covers design, validation checklist, and automation tasks needed to land the guardrails and a first-pass compatibility matrix for supported combos.
acceptance_criteria: A human-readable compatibility grid (CSV and markdown) mapping Terraform core versions to provider versions (aws, azurerm, google, random, null) and the module versions we maintain is published to Confluence
CI job that verifies module plan/apply against a pinned provider set (using tflock or provider_installation & dependency lock) for each supported combo is present in our infra repo
Provider lockfile strategy documented and implemented: per-module lockfile plus a repo-level lockfile generator; automation to refresh lockfiles under review policy
Automated health-check job that simulates a private-vpc upgrade (plan-only) across representative customer fixture stacks runs on every provider or Terraform core version bump PR
Rollout & rollback playbook for provider upgrades with canary cohort definition and monitoring hooks included in runbook
tasks: Inventory current module dependencies and record existing provider_version constraints across private-vpc modules
Create initial compatibility grid CSV mapping: terraform_core_version, aws_provider_range, azurerm_provider_range, google_provider_range, module_compat_notes
Draft provider lockfile policy: use dependency_lock.json (repo-level) and vendorized module-level .terraform.lock.hcl for deterministic CI
Implement CI matrix job (plan-only) that iterates compatibility grid combos and fails on diffs or provider plugin mismatches
Add health-check smoke fixtures that exercise: vpc creation, route tables, security groups, node pools (if GKE/AKS), and IAM changes
Define canary cohorts and monitoring SLOs (deployment success rate, plan delta token counts, error rate) for rolling provider upgrades
Author runbook with steps: prepare branch, pin versions, open upgrade PR, run CI matrix, run canary on dedicated staging cluster, monitor console metrics, promote or rollback
notes: Trade-offs considered: strict pinning reduces surprise but increases maintenance cost; this design opts for pinned ranges with scheduled, automated refresh and human review rather than wildcard pins.
We will prefer range pins (>=, <) for minor/patch automation and exact pins for providers with known backwards-incompatible history.

We will maintain a generator script that emits module-level .terraform.lock.hcl files by running init with plugin_download_dir and committed under a lock refresh PR cadence (weekly for low-risk, on-change for critical security fixes).

Observed incidents: PROD-2025-11 provider aws v4.x -> v5.0 implicit API change required immediate rollback; this motivates conservative major version pinning and pre-release CI against next-major provider candidates.

runbook: Pre-upgrade: lock current provider versions and snapshot current state; notify customers on dedicated capacity upgrade windows
Canary: run matrix plan against 5 representative customer fixtures (small, medium, large, govcompliant, onprem) and hold for 24h
Promote: if canary green and no semantic diffs, run staged promotion to remaining cohorts; otherwise rollback lockfile to previous commit and open investigation
Rollback: revert provider pins and restore previous plan-lock snapshot; if state drift occurred, coordinate with SRE to run targeted remediation runs
test_plan: Unit: validate compatibility grid parser and generator scripts with mocked provider metadata
Integration: CI matrix runs plan-only across all combos; failures generate issue with detailed plan diff
End-to-end: run plan+apply in dedicated ephemeral AWS and GCP test accounts for each provider major version under review
Chaos: simulate provider plugin download failures and verify graceful CI failure and retry behavior
